accessibility.selectDyesToSeeAnalysis: Select dyes to see accessibility analysis
accessibility.verySimular: Very similar - may be hard to distinguish
accessibility.somewhatSimilar: Similar - some users may have difficulty distinguishing
accessibility.redGreenWarning: Red-green colorblind users may see this as a different color
accessibility.tritanopiaWarning: May be hard to see for tritanopia (blue-yellow colorblindness)
accessibility.achromatopsiaWarning: May be hard to see for total colorblindness
accessibility.worstHint: The dot is the worst pair under that lens.
accessibility.unitPctDesc: The app's own measure: straight-line RGB distance between the two simulated colours, over the 441.67 diagonal of the colour cube.
accessibility.unitPctCaveat: Not a WCAG rating and not perceptual — it reads high for dark colours. Useful for ranking, not for a compliance claim.
accessibility.unitRatioDesc: WCAG relative luminance contrast between the two simulated colours. Success Criterion 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast asks for at least 3:1 between adjacent meaningful colours.
accessibility.unitRatioCaveat: This is the only readout here backed by a published standard — but it only sees lightness, so two equally bright dyes score badly even when hue tells them apart.
accessibility.unitDeDesc: CIEDE2000 colour difference between the two simulated colours — the same metric the other tools use for match quality. Around 1.0 is the smallest difference a trained eye can see.
accessibility.unitDeCaveat: Perceptually honest and consistent with the rest of the app, but no standard defines a pass mark — the cuts here are the app's calibrated separation bands, shared across its tools.
accessibility.visionDescNormal: Standard colour perception — the palette as you painted it.
accessibility.visionDescDeuteranopia: Red-green. The most common form, and about one man in twelve.
accessibility.visionDescProtanopia: Red-green, with reds darkened as well as shifted.
accessibility.visionDescTritanopia: Blue-yellow. Rare, and it hits teals and yellows hardest.
accessibility.visionDescAchromatopsia: No colour at all — only lightness separates two dyes.

comparison.selectAtLeastTwoDyes: Select at least 2 dyes to compare
comparison.subSame: {w} apart, and the match line sits at {thr}. Nobody will see the difference on a chest piece — so this is a price question, not a colour one.
comparison.subClose: {w} apart. Side by side you can just about tell; at arm's length, on cloth, you cannot.
comparison.subWide: {w} apart. These read as two different dyes at any distance.
comparison.costSame: Both cost the same from the same source, so there is nothing to save here.
comparison.costDiff: {cheap} is the cheaper of the two by {saving}.
comparison.costUnknown: {a} is a vendor dye; {b} has no vendor price and has to be found.
comparison.mCiede2000Desc: CIEDE2000 colour difference — the same metric the Extractor and Gradient Builder use to score a match. Around 1.0 is the smallest difference a trained eye can see; under 5 reads as the same colour on armour.
comparison.mCiede2000Caveat: Perceptually honest and consistent with the rest of the app, but no standard sets the line between “same” and “different” — the 5 and 10 here are this tool's call and adjustable in Advanced.
comparison.mOklabDesc: Euclidean distance in OKLab, printed raw to three decimals. OKLab is already in this codebase — it is one of the Dye Mixer's six blending models — so nothing new has to be written.
comparison.mOklabCaveat: Perceptually close to ΔE2000 at a fraction of the arithmetic, and better behaved for blues — which matters for a set like this one. Newer, so fewer published thresholds to lean on.
comparison.mCie76Desc: Straight-line distance in CIE Lab — the original 1976 formula, with none of the lightness, chroma and hue corrections ΔE2000 adds. Cheap, stable, and still the most widely implemented.
comparison.mCie76Caveat: Over-reports differences in saturated blues and under-reports them in near-neutrals — the exact failure that produced ΔE2000. Useful to show how much of a gap is formula rather than colour.
comparison.mRedmeanDesc: RGB distance with the channels weighted by how red the pair is on average — the low-cost approximation that gets most of the way to a perceptual result without leaving RGB.
comparison.mRedmeanCaveat: A clear improvement on raw RGB distance for the same cost, and the honest upgrade path if leaving RGB is off the table. Still not a colour space — it just guesses better.
comparison.mRgbDesc: Straight-line distance between the two colours in the RGB cube, 0 to 441.67. This is what the old Statistics panel reported as “Avg Distance”, with no unit printed beside it.
comparison.mRgbCaveat: Not perceptual: it treats a step in dark blue the same as a step in bright yellow, so it under-reports differences among dark dyes exactly like this set. Kept because it is what shipped.
comparison.mDistinguishDesc: The same RGB distance divided by the 441.67 diagonal of the colour cube and shown as a percentage — the number the Accessibility Checker reports for a pair.
comparison.mDistinguishCaveat: Shares every weakness of RGB distance and adds a percent sign that invites false precision. Useful only for lining this tool up against the Accessibility Checker — never as a WCAG rating.

welcome.title: Welcome to XIV Dye Tools
welcome.intro: Every dye in the game, measured. Pick a colour you want and the tools tell you which of the 125 dyes actually gets you there — and what it costs.

lead.harmony: Start from one dye and get the four or five that go with it.
lead.extractor: Upload a screenshot; get the closest dye for every colour in it.
lead.mixer: Blend two dyes to see what sits between them, then buy the nearest.
lead.gradient: Build a ramp between two dyes — every step is a dye you can wear.

welcome.tip1: Any dye slot also takes a plain hex code, so you can match something that is not in the game.
welcome.tip2: Every result is a link. Share it and it opens on the same dye for everyone.
